sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A PROMINENT UPPER TROUGH WILL CONTINUE TO ADVANCE INLAND AND OVER THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST THROUGH TONIGHT. DOWNSTREAM OF THIS TROUGH...AND TO THE NORTH OF A BUILDING SOUTH-CENTRAL/SOUTHEAST CONUS UPPER RIDGE...A SEMI-AMPLIFIED/MODERATELY STRONG BELT OF WESTERLIES WILL EXTEND FROM THE NORTHERN ROCKIES TO THE GREAT LAKES AND NEW ENGLAND.

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST/UPPER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: A WARM FRONT...EXTENDING IN THE PREDAWN HOURS ACROSS SOUTHEAST MN SOUTHEASTWARD INTO NORTHERN PORTIONS OF IL/IN...WILL CONTINUE TO SLOWLY SPREAD NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE UPPER MS RIVER VALLEY/GREAT LAKES DURING THE DAY. MEANWHILE...A COLD FRONT...WHICH IS AUGMENTED BY AN OVERNIGHT DECAYING MCS ACROSS THE EASTERN DAKOTAS/NORTHWEST MN...WILL CONTINUE TO SPREAD EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS MN TOWARD NORTH/CENTRAL WI AND THE MI UPPER PENINSULA THROUGH TONIGHT. ASIDE FROM SOME CLOUD DEBRIS FROM THE AFOREMENTIONED DECAYING MCS...STRONG DIURNAL HEATING/GRADUAL MOISTENING IS EXPECTED WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR...WITH MIDDLE/UPPER 60S F SURFACE DEWPOINTS BECOMING INCREASINGLY COMMON BY AFTERNOON/EVENING. A CONVECTIVELY ENHANCED/MCV-RELATED IMPULSE...WITH 35-50 KT MID-LEVEL WINDS NOTED IN 12Z OBSERVED SOUNDINGS AND WSR-88D VWP DATA ACROSS THE EASTERN DAKOTAS...WILL SPREAD EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD TODAY AND REACH THE LAKE SUPERIOR VICINITY BY LATE AFTERNOON/EVENING. ASIDE FROM AN INCREASINGLY UNSTABLE/UNINHIBITED BOUNDARY LAYER...THIS IMPULSE WILL BE A FACTOR FOR WHAT SHOULD BE AN INCREASE IN STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT BY MID/LATE-AFTERNOON...INITIALLY ACROSS EAST-CENTRAL MN INTO FAR WESTERN/N

sections.title: MT
sections.text: 12Z OBSERVED SOUNDINGS AND SURFACE OBSERVATIONS SUGGEST THAT SOME BOUNDARY LAYER DRYING HAS OCCURRED ACROSS MT IN THE WAKE OF YESTERDAYS STORMS...WHICH CURRENTLY LIMITS CONFIDENCE IN A HIGHER-CALIBER SEVERE RISK. NONETHELESS...LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE SHOULD RECOVER/ADVECT WESTWARD TOWARD WEST-CENTRAL MT THROUGH THE DAY. WHILE SOME HEIGHT RISES WILL OCCUR DURING THE DAY OWING TO THE AMPLIFICATION OF THE UPSTREAM PACIFIC NORTHWEST UPPER TROUGH...AT LEAST WEAK HEIGHT FALLS SHOULD OVERSPREAD THE REGION LATER THIS AFTERNOON AND TONIGHT. AS BOUNDARY-LAYER MOISTURE GRADUALLY INCREASES...AT LEAST GLANCING DPVA AND LOW-LEVEL UPSLOPE FLOW WILL CONTRIBUTE TO INCREASING STRONG THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON PARTICULARLY ACROSS WEST-CENTRAL MT. STRENGTHENING FLOW ALOFT WILL RESULT IN 50-60 KT OF DEEP-LAYER SHEAR...AND LONG HODOGRAPHS IN FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST ISOLATED SUPERCELL STORMS CAN BE EXPECTED WITH LARGE HAIL AND POSSIBLY A TORNADO OR TWO. DAMAGING WINDS MAY ALSO POSE A RISK AS STORMS SPREAD EAST-NORTHEASTWARD THIS EVENING.

sections.title: WEST TX
sections.text: WITHIN A MODESTLY FORCED/WEAKLY SHEARED FLOW REGIME...SUFFICIENT MOISTURE/INSTABILITY MAY ALLOW FOR SOME STRONGER PULSE-TYPE STORMS CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS/HAIL THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. ..GUYER/LEITMAN.. 06/10/2016

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST INTO THE WESTERN GREAT LAKES
sections.text: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SHOWS A SHORT WAVE TROUGH MOVING THROUGH THE UPPER RIDGE OVER THE NRN PLAINS/UPPER MS VALLEY. THIS LOW AMPLITUDE FEATURE IS FORECAST BY THE LATEST MODEL RUNS TO PROGRESS EWD OVER LAKE SUPERIOR/UPPER MI/NRN WI BY THIS EVENING BEFORE TURNING SEWD AND REACHING THE LOWER LAKES BY THE END OF THE PERIOD. AT THE SURFACE...THE PRIMARY NE-SW ORIENTED LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE BOUNDARY IS LOCATED FROM NORTH-CENTRAL MN SWWD INTO ERN SD...AND AS THIS BOUNDARY MOVES SEWD IT WILL LIKELY TO SERVE AS A PRIMARY FOCUS FROM STRONG/SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. A WARM FRONT EXTENDING FROM CENTRAL MN SEWD ACROSS SRN LAKE MI IS EXPECTED TO LIFT NEWD THIS AFTERNOON...WITH WARM SECTOR DEW POINTS OF 65-70F SPREADING INTO PARTS OF MN AND WI. 12Z AREA RAOBS EXHIBITED STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...AND WHEN COMBINED WITH DIURNAL HEATING WILL RESULT IN A MODERATELY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT WITH MLCAPE OF 2000-2500 J/KG. A BAND OF STORMS HAS BEEN SLOWLY DEVELOPING OVER CENTRAL MN ALONG THE AFOREMENTIONED BOUNDARY AND RECENT CAM GUIDANCE INDICATE THIS ACTIVITY WILL INTENSIFY BY EARLY AFTERNOON AS IT MOVES INTO THE EXPANDING WARM SECTOR. sections.title: MT
sections.text: A VIGOROUS UPPER LOW ALONG THE PACIFIC NW COAST IS MOVING SLOWLY EWD AND IS FORECAST TO MOVE INTO BC/WA/OREGON BY TONIGHT. STRONG SWLY WINDS ALOFT AHEAD OF THE LOW HAVE SPREAD ACROSS THE PACIFIC NW AND NRN INTERMOUNTAIN REGION...AND WILL CONTINUE EWD INTO WRN AND CENTRAL MT THROUGH TONIGHT. SEVERE CONVECTION ON THURSDAY HAD TEMPORARILY MODIFIED THE ENVIRONMENT OVER PARTS OF MT...BUT OBSERVATIONAL DATA INDICATE THAT LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE IS RETURNING WWD INTO CENTRAL MT WITH SATELLITE-DERIVED PW VALUES GREATER THAN 0.75 INCHES. VISIBLE IMAGERY SHOWS GENERALLY CLEAR SKIES OVER MOST OF MT WHICH WILL SUPPORT STRONG DIABATIC HEATING AND AIR MASS DESTABILIZATION THIS AFTERNOON WITH MUCAPE REACHING 1000-1500 J/KG. DYNAMIC FORCING FOR LARGE SCALE ASCENT DOWNSTREAM FROM THE UPPER LOW COUPLED WITH FRONTAL CONVERGENCE AND OROGRAPHIC LIFT WILL SERVE TO INITIATE CONVECTIVE STORMS OVER WRN/CENTRAL MT BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON. VEERING WIND PROFILES WITH HEIGHT BENEATH STRONG SWLY FLOW ALOFT WILL CREATE STRONG VERTICAL SHEAR OF 40-50 KT IN THE LOWEST 6 KM AGL FAVORABLE FOR ORGANIZED CONVECTIVE STRUCTURES INCLUDING SUPERCELLS. THE STRONGER CELLS WILL BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING VERY LARGE HAIL AND STRONG WIN

sections.title: DISCUSSION
sections.text: THE ONLY SUBSTANTIAL CHANGES MADE TO THIS OUTLOOK UPDATE INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: 1) MOVED THE SEVERE PROBABILITIES COINCIDENT WITH THE BAND OF STORMS OVER THE UPPER MIDWEST. 2) REINTRODUCED 5-PERCENT TORNADO PROBABILITIES OVER N-CNTRL WI NWD INTO THE WRN PARTS OF THE UPPER PENINSULA OF MICH. 3) REMOVED 5-PERCENT TORNADO PROBABILITIES OVER CNTRL MT. 4) MOVED 5-PERCENT WIND PROBABILITIES TO BE NEAR THE HIGHER TERRAIN IN SWRN TX WHERE STORM COVERAGE APPEARS HIGHEST. 5) ADDED 5-PERCENT WIND PROBABILITIES FOR STORMS DEVELOPING OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN IN SERN AZ ON THE NERN PERIPHERY OF A MCV LOCATED NEAR THE N SHORE OF THE GULF OF CA. EFFECTIVE SHEAR 30-40 KT AIDED IN PART BY LOW-LEVEL WLY/S BENEATH 30 KT H5 FLOW WILL POTENTIALLY AID IN STORM ORGANIZATION AS STORMS MOVE NWWD INTO THE LOWER DESERTS NEAR PHOENIX TOWARDS EARLY EVENING. VERY STEEP 0-2 KM LAPSE RATES AND 50S DEWPOINTS WILL SUPPORT AN ISOLD MICROBURST/WIND DAMAGE THREAT THIS EVENING. ..SMITH.. 06/10/2016 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1133 AM CDT FRI JUN 10 2016/

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A POTENTIAL FOR WIND DAMAGE AND ISOLATED LARGE HAIL WILL LIKELY DEVELOP ACROSS PARTS OF THE UPPER MS VALLEY EARLY THIS AFTERNOON. WW ISSUANCE WILL PROBABLY BE NEEDED ACROSS THE REGION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A COLD FRONT OVER WRN MN EXTENDING SWWD INTO NE SD WITH A 1005 MB LOW OVER SCNTRL MN. A WARM FRONT EXTENDS EWD FROM THE SFC LOW INTO WRN WI WITH SFC WINDS LOCALLY BACKED TO THE SOUTH SOUTHEAST JUST TO THE NORTH OF THE FRONT. A MOIST AIRMASS IS IN PLACE AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT WITH SFC DEWPOINTS GENERALLY IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S F. ACCORDING TO MESOSCALE ANALYSIS...A POCKET OF MODERATE INSTABILITY IS LOCATED FROM NEAR THE SFC LOW IN SCNTRL MN EXTENDING SEWD INTO WRN WI. A COUPLE OF LINES OF THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING AHEAD OF THE FRONT IN CNTRL AND NE MN. THE WRF-HRRR SUGGEST THIS ACTIVITY WILL GRADUALLY INTENSIFY AND MOVE EWD ACROSS ERN MN INTO NW WI THIS AFTERNOON. REGIONAL WSR-88D VWPS ALONG THIS CORRIDOR SHOW WIND PROFILES WITH STRONG VEERING WITH HEIGHT IN THE LOW-LEVELS AND 40 TO 50 KT OF FLOW ABOVE 3 KM. THIS SHOULD SUPPORT A SEVERE THREAT AS A LINEAR CONVECTIVE SYSTEM INTENSIFIES THIS AFTERNOON. WIND DAMAGE WILL BE MOST LIKELY WITH BOWING SEGMENTS ALONG THE LINE. HAIL WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGER CORES EMBEDDED IN THE LINE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A SEVERE THREAT APPEARS LIKELY TO DEVELOP ACROSS SRN MN EWD INTO WRN AND CNTRL WI. WIND DAMAGE AND ISOLATED LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE AS CELLS GRADUALLY INTENSIFY. WW ISSUANCE WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED ACROSS THE REGION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A COLD FRONT MOVING SEWD ACROSS SCNTRL MN WITH CONVECTION DEVELOPING ALONG THE FRONT. AHEAD OF THE FRONT...MODERATE INSTABILITY IS ANALYZED WITH MLCAPE NOW ESTIMATED IN THE 2000 TO 3000 J/KG RANGE. A CAPPING INVERSION IS DIMINISHING WHICH WILL ALLOW FOR SFC-BASED DEVELOPMENT TO INCREASE OVER THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS. THE INSTABILITY COMBINED WITH 0-6 KM SHEAR OF 30 TO 35 KT EVIDENT ON THE LACROSSE WI WSR-88D VWP SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR STORM ROTATION AND ISOLATED LARGE HAIL. IN ADDITION...THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER WITH SFC DEWPOINTS NEAR 70 F ALONG WITH DIRECTIONAL TURNING OF THE WINDS WITH HEIGHT IN THE LOW-LEVELS AND STEEP LAPSE RATES SHOULD SUPPORT A WIND DAMAGE THREAT AS WELL.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTM INITIATION IS EXPECTED DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. ONCE INITIATION OCCURS...THE OVERALL ENVIRONMENT IS FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. TRENDS ACROSS THE REGION WILL BE MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SWLY FLOW ALOFT HAS BEEN INCREASING ACROSS THE REGION OVER THE PAST FEW HOURS /AS NOTED IN THE 18Z TFX RAOB/ AS THE PACIFIC NW UPPER LOW CONTINUES TO SLOWLY MOVE EWD. ORIENTATION OF THIS FLOW ALOFT IS FAVORABLE FOR ENHANCED OROGRAPHIC ASCENT THROUGHOUT THE NRN ROCKIES. THIS OROGRAPHIC LIFT COMBINED WITH INCREASING LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH THE UPPER LOW /AND AN EMBEDDED SHORTWAVE MOVING QUICKLY THROUGH ITS BASE/ WILL PERSIST ACROSS THE REGION. THIS PERSISTENT LIFT WILL ACT TO ERODE THE CAPPING INVERSION OBSERVED ON THE 18Z TFX SOUNDING AND INCREASING LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE AND STRONG SURFACE HEATING WILL EVENTUALLY RESULT IN CONVECTIVE INITIATION. TIMING OF THIS INITIATION AND RESULTING TSTM COVERAGE ARE A BIT UNCERTAIN...LARGELY A RESULT OF THE AMOUNT OF AIRMASS MODIFICATION NEEDED TO SUPPORT CONVECTION. RECENT HIGH-RESOLUTION GUIDANCE HAS NOT SHOWN GOOD CONSENSUS AND THE MOST RECENT PARALLEL HRRR RUN HOLDS OFF MOST ACTIVITY UNTIL AFTER 00Z AND EVEN THEN KEEPS STORM COVERAGE ISOLATED. HOWEVER...RECENT VISIBLE SATELLITE TRENDS SUGGEST EARLIER STORM INITIATION. GIVEN THE STRONGLY SHEARED ENVIRONMENT /I.E. 0-6 KM BULK SHEAR ABOVE 60 KT ON THE 18Z TFX SOUNDING/...SUPERCELLS ARE LIKELY ONCE INITIATION OCCURS...PARTICULARLY TOWARDS CNTRL MT WHERE THE MORE FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT EXISTS. PRIMARY SVR THREATS ARE VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. HIGH LCLS AND MODEST LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE WILL LIMIT THE TORNADO THREAT. TRENDS ACROSS THE REGION WILL BE MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE WATCH....ALTHOUGH UNCERTAINTY REGARDING STORM COVERAGE PRECLUDES HIGHER WATCH PROBABILITIES.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE DURING THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS AS TSTMS DEVELOP OVER SE AZ AND MOVE NWWD TOWARDS THE PHOENIX METRO AREA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT SATELLITE AND RADAR IMAGERY SHOW TSTM DEVELOPMENT OFF THE HIGHER TERRAIN IN SE AZ WITH ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT POSSIBLE AS ELY FLOW ALOFT PERSISTS. THIS AREA OF SLIGHTLY STRONGER ELY FLOW /SAMPLED WELL BY THE EMX VAD/ ATOP WLY SURFACE FLOW IS SUPPORTING MODEST BULK SHEAR /AROUND 30-35 KNOTS FROM 0-6 KM PER THE LATEST MESOANALYSIS AND EMX VAD/. THIS FAVORABLE KINEMATIC ENVIRONMENT IS JUXTAPOSED WITH MODEST INSTABILITY AND SOME MORE ORGANIZED/PERSISTENT STORM STRUCTURES MAY RESULT. DOWNDRAFT POTENTIAL WITH THE MORE ORGANIZED/PERSISTENT STORMS IS HIGH...PARTICULARLY AS STORMS MOVE NWWD TOWARDS THE PHOENIX AREA.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT CONTINUES FOR REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF TORNADO WATCH 242...AND A NEW WATCH MAY BE NEEDED PRIOR TO 23Z FOR AREAS EAST AND SOUTHEAST OF THE CURRENT WATCH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TWO DISTINCT AREAS OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WERE IN PROGRESS AT 22Z ACROSS WW 242. THE FIRST WAS OVER NORTHEAST WISCONSIN FROM LINCOLN COUNTY NORTHWARD TO IRON COUNTY MICHIGAN...WHERE A WELL-DEVELOPED BOWING SEGMENT WITH A HISTORY OF DAMAGING WINDS CONTINUES MOVING EAST AT AROUND 45 MPH. STRONG STORMS EXTENDED NORTH INTO THE KEWEENAW PENINSULA...WHERE SURFACE-BASED INSTABILITY WAS LOWER. FARTHER SOUTH...SEVERE STORMS EXTENDED FROM EAU CLAIRE COUNTY SOUTHWEST INTO WW 243. LATEST MESOANALYSIS SHOWS THE NORTHERN AREA OF SEVERE STORMS TRAVERSING THE INSTABILITY GRADIENT IN THE PRESENCE OF 35 KTS OF WESTERLY VERTICAL SHEAR. FARTHER SOUTH...STRONG SURFACE-BASED INSTABILITY IS IN PLACE WITH MLCAPE OF 2500-3000 J/KG...HOWEVER DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WAS BELOW 30 KTS. OVERALL...BOTH AREAS OF STORMS WILL LIKELY CONTINUE MOVING EAST OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS WITH A CONTINUED THREAT FOR MAINLY DAMAGING WINDS...AND PERHAPS A TORNADO ASSOCIATED WITH THE MORE PRONOUNCED BOWING SEGMENTS. A NEW WATCH MAY BE NEEDED BY 23Z FOR AREAS EAST INTO THE DOOR PENINSULA EXTENDING SOUTHWARD TO THE EAST OF WW 243.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND ISOLATED HAIL CONTINUES FOR THE REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH 243.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WITH A HISTORY OF SEVERE WINDS/DAMAGE WERE LOCATED FROM JACKSON COUNTY WI SOUTHWEST TO EMMET COUNTY IA AT 2245Z. THESE STORMS WERE LOCATED WITHIN AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY STRONG SURFACE-BASED INSTABILITY BUT MODEST /BELOW 30 KTS/ VERTICAL WIND SHEAR. RECENT RADAR TRENDS SUGGEST THE GUST FRONT HAS SURGED OUT WELL AHEAD OF THE STORMS OVER FAR SOUTHEAST MN...SOMEWHAT DIMINISHING THE SEVERE THREAT AT LEAST IN THE SHORT TERM IN THIS AREA. OVERALL...WITH MODERATE-STRONG INSTABILITY IN PLACE AND A PRONOUNCED COLD POOL...EXPECT THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS TO CONTINUE ACROSS THE REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF THE WATCH THROUGH 02Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND THREAT CONTINUES ACROSS WW 244 WITH ONGOING THUNDERSTORMS. AN ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT IS INCREASING ACROSS PORTIONS OF WW 244 AND DOWNSTREAM INTO ERN MT...AND A SMALL TORNADO WATCH MAY BE NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT RADAR IMAGERY AS OF 2315Z DEPICTS A PAIR OF SUPERCELLS EXTENDING FROM NWRN FERGUS INTO N-CNTRL JUDITH BASIN COUNTIES IN CNTRL MT. SFC OBSERVATIONS SHOW A WARM FRONT EXTENDING ACROSS CNTRL/ERN MT...WITH SELY TO ELY FLOW OCCURRING ALONG AND S OF THIS FRONT. 23Z OBSERVATION FROM KLWT HAS A SELY SUSTAINED WIND OF 19KT GUSTING TO 29KT...AND 23Z RAP MESOANALYSIS ESTIMATES EFFECTIVE SRH OF 200-300 M2/S2 IS PRESENT ALONG/E OF THE ONGOING PAIR OF SUPERCELLS. WITH SUFFICIENT LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE IN PLACE S OF THE WARM FRONT...AND STRONG MID-LEVEL FLOW EXPECTED TO CONTINUE OVER THE MCD AREA...SUPERCELL STRUCTURES WITH AN ATTENDANT LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WIND RISK AND ISOLATED TORNADO RISK SHOULD CONTINUE FOR AT LEAST THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. SOME INCREASE IN THE SELY LOW-LEVEL FLOW CENTERED AROUND 850 MB IS EXPECTED THROUGH 04Z ACROSS PARTS OF CNTRL/ERN MT DOWNSTREAM OF ONGOING CONVECTION...WHICH WOULD FURTHER SUPPORT AN ISOLATED TORNADO RISK...MAINLY IN JUDITH BASIN...FERGUS...SOUTHERN PHILLIPS...AND PETROLEUM COUNTIES. A SMALL TORNADO WATCH MAY NEED TO BE CONSIDERED OVER THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS DEPENDING ON CONVECTIVE TRENDS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORMS MOVING EAST/SOUTHEAST ACROSS WESTERN LOWER MICHIGAN THIS EVENING MAY PRODUCE LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS THROUGH 03-04Z. ALTHOUGH A WATCH IS NOT ANTICIPATED...TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LINE OF STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE CENTRAL UPPER PENINSULA OF MI INTO NORTHEAST WI WILL MOVE EAST/SOUTHEAST AT 40-45 MPH...CROSSING LAKE MICHIGAN AND AFFECTING WESTERN LOWER MICHIGAN AFTER 01Z. ALTHOUGH AN OVERALL WEAKENING TREND IS EXPECTED AS THE STORMS CROSS LAKE MICHIGAN AND MOVE INTO A MORE MARGINAL THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT...THE FORWARD SPEED OF THE STORMS MAY TEND TO LESSEN THE INFLUENCE OF RELATIVELY COOL LAKE WATER TEMPERATURES /MID-UPPER 50S/ AS THE STORMS MOVE EAST. GIVEN THIS SCENARIO...AND THE POTENTIAL FOR NEW UPDRAFTS TO DEVELOP ALONG THE GUST FRONT OR IN ADVANCE OF THE LINE...AT LEAST SOME POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED STRONG/BRIEFLY SEVERE WIND GUSTS WILL EXIST ACROSS THE DISCUSSION AREA UNTIL AROUND 03-04Z. ALTHOUGH A WW IS NOT EXPECTED...CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND STRONG TO LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND THREAT SHOULD CONTINUE FOR THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. WW ISSUANCE IS NOT EXPECTED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED OVER THE PAST TWO HOURS ACROSS PARTS OF CNTRL/WRN NEB ALONG A WEAK FRONTAL BOUNDARY. THE AIRMASS ACROSS MUCH OF THE MCD AREA IS STRONGLY UNSTABLE...WITH MLCAPE AOA 1500 J/KG AS SFC DEWPOINTS ARE GENERALLY IN THE MID 60S AND TEMPERATURES HAVE WARMED INTO THE MID 90S. STEEP LOW AND MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE PRESENT ACROSS NEB PER 12Z LBF SOUNDING AND RAP FORECAST SOUNDINGS...SUPPORTING THE STRONG INSTABILITY. FLOW/SHEAR ACROSS THIS REGION REMAINS WEAK HOWEVER...WHICH SHOULD ACT TO LIMIT STORM LONGEVITY. RECENT RADAR IMAGERY SHOWS NUMEROUS OUTFLOWS EMANATING FROM THE ISOLATED CONVECTION...WHICH MAY ACT TO INITIATE SOME ADDITIONAL THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO. ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND STRONG TO LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS UNTIL DIURNAL COOLING AND INCREASING MLCIN ACT TO DIMINISH CONVECTIVE COVERAGE/INTENSITY AFTER 02Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL CONTINUE TO POSE A RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS...MAINLY OVER SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH 245. THE SEVERE THREAT OVER THE REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH 243 CONTINUES TO DIMINISH AND A DOWNSTREAM WATCH IS NOT EXPECTED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LINE OF STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS EXTENDED FROM NEAR GREEN BAY SOUTH/WEST TO DANE COUNTY WI THEN WEST ACROSS NORTHERN IA. THE GREATEST SEVERE THREAT CONTINUES OVER SOUTHERN PORTIONS OF WW 245 ...WHERE A WELL ORGANIZED BOWING SEGMENT WITH ATTENDANT COLD POOL CONTINUES MOVING SOUTHEAST WITHIN A MODERATE/STRONGLY UNSTABLE AIR MASS. DESPITE NOCTURNAL COOLING/INCREASING INHIBITION THESE STORMS WILL POSE A CONTINUED SEVERE WIND RISK...WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR ADDITIONAL BRIEF QLCS CIRCULATIONS AS RECENTLY OCCURRED OVER OUTAGAMIE COUNTY. FARTHER WEST ACROSS WW 243...STORMS HAVE GENERALLY WEAKENED WITH SOUTHWARD MOVEMENT AS INHIBITION INCREASES. WEST OF WW 243...A LOCALIZED SEVERE THREAT CONTINUES WITH CELLS THAT HAVE DEVELOPED ON THE WESTERN FLANK OF STORM OUTFLOW. THESE STORMS WILL POSE A SEVERE THREAT FOR AT LEAST A COUPLE MORE HOURS...BUT THE OVERALL SEVERE THREAT OVER WW 243 SHOULD CONTINUE TO DIMINISH. THUS...A NEW WATCH IS NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED. ..BUNTING.. 06/11/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND THREAT CONTINUES ACROSS MAINLY ERN PORTIONS OF WW 244. A LOCAL EXTENSION OF THE SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH IN SPACE AND/OR TIME MAY BE NEEDED ACROSS PARTS OF ERN MT DEPENDING ON HOW THUNDERSTORMS EVOLVE OVER THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR IMAGERY SHOWS THAT INITIAL SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT ACROSS CNTRL MT EARLIER THIS AFTERNOON HAS EVOLVED INTO MULTIPLE CLUSTERS WITH EMBEDDED MID-LEVEL CIRCULATIONS. GIVEN A CONTINUED FAVORABLE INSTABILITY/SHEAR PARAMETER SPACE ALONG AND S OF A WARM FRONT DRAPED ACROSS CNTRL/ERN MT...ONGOING CONVECTIVE ACTIVITY SHOULD CONTINUE TO POSE MAINLY A LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND RISK THROUGH THE SCHEDULED 04Z EXPIRATION OF WW 244. LOW-LEVEL SHEAR REMAINS FAVORABLE ACROSS SRN/ERN PORTIONS OF THE WW...BUT INCREASING MLCIN AND LESS FAVORABLE STORM MODES SUGGEST THE ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT MAY BE DECREASING SOMEWHAT. WITH DIURNAL COOLING OF THE BOUNDARY LAYER OCCURRING OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS...IT IS NOT CLEAR HOW LONG A SEVERE THREAT WILL CONTINUE ACROSS MAINLY ERN MT. DEPENDING ON CONVECTIVE TRENDS...A LOCAL EXTENSION IN SPACE AND/OR TIME MAY BE NEEDED FOR SEVERAL COUNTIES IN ERN MT. ..GLEASON.. 06/11/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A CONFINED/ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT MAY DEVELOP INTO PARTS OF WESTERN ND DURING THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS...BUT OVERALL RISK SHOULD DIMINISH AND A NEW WW ISSUANCE IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A SMALL CLUSTER CENTERED OVER DAWSON COUNTY MT HAS HAD A HISTORY OF SEVERE WIND GUSTS...MOST RECENTLY A SPOTTER MEASURED GUST OF 62 MPH AT 0535Z. THIS CLUSTER IS OCCURRING AROUND 100 MILES NORTH OF THE SURFACE WARM FRONT OVER SOUTHEAST MT THAT ARCS EAST OF A CYCLONE IN THE LEE OF THE BIG HORN MOUNTAINS. DOWNSTREAM AIR MASS IS MORE STABLE INTO WEST-CENTRAL/SOUTHWEST ND WHERE SURFACE TEMPERATURES ARE AROUND 8-15 DEG F COOLER COMPARED TO EAST-CENTRAL MT. THIS SUGGESTS CONVECTION SHOULD GRADUALLY WEAKEN THIS MORNING AS IT SPREADS EAST INTO ND...A SCENARIO WELL SUPPORTED BY RECENT CONVECTION-ALLOWING SIMULATIONS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A SWATH OF SEVERE HAIL IS POSSIBLE THROUGH ABOUT 13-14Z BEFORE FAST-MOVING ELEVATED STORMS LIKELY PROGRESS INTO SASKATCHEWAN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A COUPLE OF ELEVATED CELLS HAVE RECENTLY INTENSIFIED NEAR/NORTH OF THE GREAT FALLS AREA...YIELDING HAIL REPORTED UP TO 1.5 INCH IN DIAMETER. THIS ACTIVITY APPEARS TO BE AIDED IN LARGE-SCALE ASCENT DOWNSTREAM OF A MID-LEVEL VORTICITY MAX SHIFTING NORTH ALONG THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER ACROSS THE SOUTHERN CANADIAN ROCKIES. OVERALL ENVIRONMENT IS CHARACTERIZED BY PROBABLE WEAK ELEVATED BUOYANCY...BUT A RATHER ELONGATED MID/UPPER-LEVEL HODOGRAPH GIVEN THE STRONG SPEED SHEAR SAMPLED BY TFX VWP DATA. AS SUCH...THE PRIMARY HAZARD WILL BE HAIL. CURRENT NORTHEASTERLY STORM MOTIONS AROUND 45 KT SUGGEST ACTIVITY WILL SHIFT ACROSS THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER BETWEEN 13-14Z.
